msItem.title: 43 Miracles of Mary
msItem.note: There are supplications at the beginning and the end of each miracle. The name of the original supplicant has been erased in the vast majority of supplications. The new one, written over in a different red ink, is Ḫāyla Māryām. The name of the original supplicant is Erāqlis, and his name appears on for the first time and is preserved in the rest of supplications until the end of the manuscript.

Endbands are present, the headband is slightly damaged.

history.provenance:
The manuscript contains numerous supplications for Erāqlis and Ḫāyla Māryām. The name of the latter has been added later by another hand in a different red colour. As it is evident from the ownership note, the manuscript belonged at some point to
Lady Valerie Susie Meux of Theobald’s Park, Waltham Cross, Essex. After her death in 1910 the whole collection was sold. Many of the objects, including this manuscript, were bought by William Randolph Hearst, whose collection was sold at Sotheby’s, 11–12 July 1939.
